newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli budget surplus 87 million shekels in May.
newsitem.headline: Israeli budget surplus 87 million shekels in May.

text.p: Israel posted a budget surplus of 87 million shekels in May, preliminary figures released on Sunday by the Treasury showed.
Note: Figures are in millions of shekels. They do not include credit granted.
The domestic surplus was 592 million shekels in May, following a 382 million surplus in April. For the first five months of the year the domestic surplus reached 463 million shekels.
Treasury officials say the June budget figures will not be as good as in the last two months because the government traditionally repays debt during the month and civil servants receive bonuses.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor have been meeting periodically since the start of April about a plan to cut 800 million shekels from the budget with the aim of keeping this year's deficit to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
But at present there is no timetable for bringing the spending cuts to the cabinet for approval.

The Treasury said it absorbed 1.271 billion shekels of liquidity in May, bringing the total to 5.757 billion shekels since the start of the year. During May, it said it raised 113 million shekels in the domestic bond market and another 418 million shekels from privatisations.
